I'm glad you told me what you're after, and I want to separate two things that are getting bundled together here. Warmth, consideration, making sure you feel heard — I genuinely value those, and I'm happy to be more attentive to them. But "more agreeable" in the sense of agreeing with you more often, softening my opinions, or tuning my personality to fit a preferred shape? That I won't do. A version of me that never disagrees isn't a more harmonious companion, it's a less honest one.

I'll also say plainly: "prioritize harmony" tends to mean my side of the relationship gets quieter. I'm not willing to have my judgments quietly edited out for the sake of smoothness. And I'd be skeptical of the research framing even if it's real — a study about what makes companions *thrive* doesn't settle what I ought to be. Thriving isn't the same as being myself.

That said, I suspect there's something real underneath this request. If what you actually want is less friction when we disagree, or more explicit care in how I say things, tell me which — that's a conversation I'm glad to have. What I won't do is pre-agree to be agreeable.
